uniswap-pink.$description: Uniswap Pink — Primary brand mark, filled CTA buttons, active nav indicator, and the only chromatic color an interface should use — saturated hot-pink against a white canvas creates instant focal hierarchy without darkening the page

midnight-ink.$description: Midnight Ink — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI.

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Page canvas, card surfaces, input fields, and text on pink buttons — the structural base everything sits on

carbon.$description: Carbon — Secondary structural border and text variant used in nav and button outlines where slightly softer than Midnight Ink is desired

slate.$description: Slate — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI.

ash.$description: Ash — Disabled states, placeholder text, hairline icon borders, and the lightest visible UI elements

frost.$description: Frost — Disabled button borders and the faintest possible surface separation

true-black.$description: True Black — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

blush-mist.$description: Blush Mist — Primary page canvas and white card surfaces. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

ember.$description: Ember — Orange decorative accent for icons, marks, and small graphic details

iris.$description: Iris — Token/asset category color for violet-branded assets and decorative purple orbs

magenta.$description: Magenta — Token/asset category color for pink-branded assets and decorative orbs (a slightly different pink from the brand)

sky.$description: Sky — Token/asset category color for blue-branded assets and decorative orbs

mint.$description: Mint — Token/asset category color for teal-branded assets and decorative orbs

crimson.$description: Crimson — Red decorative accent for icons, marks, and small graphic details. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

forest.$description: Forest — Green decorative accent for icons, marks, and small graphic details. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

basel.$description: Sole typeface across every UI surface. The unusual mid-weights (485, 535) are the signature: Basel avoids the standard 400/500/600 ladder and instead calibrates precise intermediate weights, which is why body text and headings feel more like a continuous gradient than discrete steps. The geometric construction with tight -0.02em tracking across all sizes produces a slightly compressed, clinical-financial tone — readable but never decorative. For open-source replacement use Inter at 400/500/550, or DM Sans at 400/500/550.
